targets.title: The Chat page
targets.description: This is a full-page chat with your agents. The name at the top shows who you're talking to. Your main agent is picked for you.

targets.title: Type a message
targets.description: Click the message box and type something. Ask a question, or tell the agent what you want done.

targets.title: Send it
targets.description: Press Enter or click the arrow to send. Shift+Enter adds a new line. While the agent replies, the arrow becomes a stop button. The paperclip attaches images.

targets.title: Or start from a suggestion
targets.description: On an empty chat these cards give you a ready-made first prompt. Clicking one sends it straight away.

targets.title: Reading replies
targets.description: Replies stream in with Markdown and code blocks. Tool calls the agent makes show up as cards you can expand to see the input and output. Hover a reply to copy or regenerate it.

targets.title: Attach files
targets.description: The paperclip adds images and videos to your message. You can also drag files onto the chat or paste a screenshot.

targets.title: Model and thinking level
targets.description: The model picker also sets the thinking level: quick answers for simple questions, deeper thinking for harder work. It applies to this chat only.

targets.title: Reply actions
targets.description: The + next to a reply opens more actions, like turning the answer into a task or a document.

targets.title: Your chat list
targets.description: Past chats live in the sidebar. Open it any time to jump back into a conversation or start a new one.

targets.title: Your chats
targets.description: Past conversations live in the chat list next to the conversation.

targets.title: Search chats
targets.description: Type to filter your chats by title.

targets.title: New chat
targets.description: New chat starts a fresh conversation with the current agent. Each chat keeps its own history, model and thinking level.

targets.title: Who you're talking to
targets.description: Click the agent name to see every agent you can chat with.
keywords: Pick the agent and the model

targets.title: Find an agent
targets.description: Type part of a name or id to filter the list.
keywords: Pick the agent and the model

targets.title: Search models
targets.description: Type a model or provider name. Filters narrows by provider, capability (vision, tools) or tier. Agent default at the top switches back.
keywords: Pick the agent and the model

targets.title: Switch agents here too
targets.description: The header shows the agent and its model. Click it to search and switch. Each agent keeps its own quick-chat thread, so switching back restores the conversation.

targets.title: Type a message
targets.description: Type in the box. Enter sends, just like on the Chat page.

targets.title: Close it
targets.description: Close the sidebar (or press Esc). Your thread is still here next time you open it.

targets.title: API keys
targets.description: Every provider key you've added is listed here, with its status. Keys are stored in this gateway's auth profile store, not in the browser.

targets.description: Guided setup has an AI brain step that picks your main model. Click it to jump there.

targets.title: Pick a provider
targets.description: On this computer runs free local models (Ollama or vLLM) and needs no key. Cloud provider needs your API key. Check key loads the live model list, and the model you save becomes your agents' main model.

targets.title: Agent Control
targets.description: The Agents page lists every agent the gateway knows about. The counts show how many are active right now, how many agents exist and how many sessions they hold.

targets.title: Your roster
targets.description: Each agent appears here. Click one to open its detail panel with its sessions, tools, skills, MCP servers, sub-agents, references and prompt.

targets.title: Status colours
targets.description: Active agents have a live session, Default is the agent that answers when none is picked, Idle agents are ready, and Offline ones are disabled.

targets.title: Refresh
targets.description: Click Refresh to reload the list from the gateway.

targets.title: New Agent
targets.description: Click New Agent to open the form.

targets.title: Pick an id
targets.description: The id is how chats, tools and other agents refer to this agent: lowercase, no spaces. Type one.

targets.title: Native or CLI
targets.description: A Native agent calls an LLM directly, with an optional model and system prompt. A CLI agent runs a command such as claude or codex as a subprocess, with its own timeout.

targets.title: Create Agent
targets.description: Create Agent adds it to your gateway config, using the workspace folder you entered. It then appears in the roster, the chat agent picker and the goal and phase agent lists.

targets.title: Close the form
targets.description: Click Cancel to throw the draft away.

targets.title: Quick config
targets.description: Click Config to open quick agent configuration.

targets.title: Pick an agent
targets.description: Every agent is listed, with a DEFAULT tag on your default. Click the first one.

targets.title: Model
targets.description: The Model tab sets this agent's model. Default inherits the global model from Setup. Changes save straight away.

targets.title: Tools, skills, sub-agents, prompt
targets.description: Tools and Skills are allowlists of what the agent may use. Sub-agents lists the agents it may spawn (empty means all). Prompt holds its custom system prompt.

targets.title: More in the detail panel
targets.description: Selecting an agent on the page opens the full panel, which adds its sessions, MCP servers, references and, for CLI agents, CLI settings.

targets.title: Close quick config
targets.description: Click × to close it.

targets.title: Follow each run
targets.description: Activity gives every parallel run its own card with live steps and output. You can open, pause or stop any of them.

targets.title: Check the results
targets.description: When a run finishes, Reviews › Oversight shows what it changed and a verified, unverified or failed verdict. Only trust results marked verified.

targets.title: Agent Activity
targets.description: Activity is the live view of everything running: sessions by type (native, sub-agent, coder) and a count of live runs. The toggles filter the list and set how often it refreshes.

targets.title: Queue events
targets.description: The gold strip at the top shows the phase queue's latest events as they happen.

targets.title: At a glance
targets.description: Active agents, work completed today, pending tasks and the average run time.

targets.title: Recently completed
targets.description: Finished runs stay here for the day. Filter by today or this week, or search them.

targets.title: Find a run
targets.description: Search by label, task or run id.

targets.title: Filter what needs you
targets.description: Filter by run status, by your review decision (pending, approved, sent back, drift detected) and time range. Needs attention shows only runs with blockers.

targets.title: Open Autonomy › Goals
targets.description: Goals is the first tab on the Autonomy page. Click it to make sure you're there.

targets.title: The New goal form
targets.description: Everything a goal run needs is on this card: the goal, the checks that prove it's done, the agent and the project folder. Click the header to fold it away when you don't need it.

targets.title: Open the form
targets.description: The form is folded. Click New goal to open it.

targets.title: Describe the goal
targets.description: Say what should be true when the agent is done. Type a goal. It stays a draft until you press Start goal.

targets.title: Done when…
targets.description: Checks decide when the goal is complete, not the agent. Command passes when it exits 0, File exists and File contains read files, AI judge reviews the output and diff, and Screenshots look right runs visual_verify.

targets.title: Pick the agent and model
targets.description: Any coding CLI or gateway agent can work on a goal. Leave the model empty to use the backend default.

targets.title: Start goal
targets.description: Start goal launches the agent in your project folder, and it keeps working until every check passes or a limit in Advanced limits is hit. You'll get a notification when it finishes.

targets.title: Your goal runs
targets.description: Every run is listed here with its status, agent, passing checks and iteration count. Runs are stored in the gateway, so they survive restarts.

targets.title: Filter by outcome
targets.description: Click Done to see only completed runs. Active shows running and paused runs, and Failed shows failed and exhausted ones.

targets.title: Back to everything
targets.description: Click All to see every run again.

targets.title: The loop
targets.description: When the agent stops, every check runs. Failing output is fed back and the same session resumes. The run ends Completed when all checks pass, Exhausted at a limit, or Failed after repeated crashes.

targets.title: Inside a run
targets.description: Select a run to see each check's latest output and pass/fail history, and every iteration with the prompt sent and the agent's output. You can pause, re-check now, retry, or add an instruction that resumes the agent.

targets.title: Run reviews
targets.description: The Reviews page lists a review for every agent run: what was built, the files touched and any issues. Select a run on the left to read its full review on the right.

targets.title: Search reviews
targets.description: Type part of a title, run id or summary to narrow the list.

targets.title: Filter by build status
targets.description: Built, Not built, Partial, Failed and Running filter the list. The time chips next to them limit it to the last hour, day or week.

targets.title: What gets checked
targets.description: Commits must exist on the run's branch, claimed files must show in the diff, and safe build or test commands are re-run. Screenshots must be real images newer than the run. Visual changes with no screenshots stay UNVERIFIED.

targets.title: Open Autonomy › Phases
targets.description: The phase queue lives on the Phases tab of the Autonomy page. Click it.

targets.title: Dispatch switch
targets.description: When dispatch is running, the queue starts eligible entries on its own. Pausing it holds everything that hasn't started yet. It's one switch for the whole queue.

targets.title: Backend health
targets.description: Each coding CLI shows whether it's ok, not logged in or not installed. Hover a chip for the fix. Re-check probes them again. A phase on a missing CLI blocks, or moves to its fallback agent.

targets.title: Find blocked entries
targets.description: Click Blocked to see entries waiting on you. It covers blocked entries and dead-letter ones that crashed repeatedly.

targets.title: Back to all entries
targets.description: Click All to see the whole queue again.

targets.title: How phased entries work
targets.description: Phases run in order. Each one completes only when the run is verified and every gate check passes, never just because the process exited. Select an entry to see each phase, its attempts and logs.

targets.title: Open the form
targets.description: Click New phased entry to open the form.

targets.title: Name the entry
targets.description: Give the whole piece of work a short title.

targets.title: Write the brief
targets.description: The brief is shared with every phase, so put the overall goal and constraints here.

targets.title: Isolation and priority
targets.description: None runs in your project folder. One worktree per entry gives the entry its own git branch. One worktree per phase branches each phase from the previous one. Higher priority entries dispatch first.

targets.title: Name the first phase
targets.description: Each phase has its own name, brief, agent, model, fallback agent, attempt limit and timeout. Type a name for phase 1.

targets.title: Add a gate check
targets.description: With no gate checks, the verification verdict alone decides. Click + Add gate check to require a command, file or AI-judge check as well.

targets.title: Gate checks
targets.description: The default gate is a Command check like pnpm test, which passes when it exits 0. You can also check a file exists, a file contains a pattern, or ask an AI judge.

targets.title: Queue it
targets.description: The Queue button adds the entry. It starts when dispatch is running and a slot is free (two at a time by default). Clear resets the form.

targets.title: Open Autonomy › Scheduled
targets.description: Scheduled agent tasks live on the Scheduled tab of the Autonomy page. Click it.

targets.title: The task list
targets.description: Each row shows the schedule, who does the review, when it runs next and how the last run went. A badge tells you when items are waiting for your decision.

targets.title: Run, pause or edit
targets.description: Select a task to see its repos and controls. Run now starts a review straight away, Pause stops the schedule and Edit changes it.

targets.title: Needs you
targets.description: Suggested items that wait for a decision land here: Approve, Modify, Reject or Snooze 24h. Run history below lists every review, with a link to its PDF in Reports.

targets.title: New task
targets.description: Click New task to open the form. Nothing is saved until you press Create.

targets.title: Name it
targets.description: Give the review a name you'll recognise in Telegram and in the run history.

targets.title: Pick a schedule
targets.description: Click a preset such as Daily 09:00, or type your own cron expression and timezone underneath.

targets.title: Repos to review
targets.description: List the repositories by path, with an optional branch. The review only reads them. Approved work happens later in a new worktree.

targets.title: Delivery and approvals
targets.description: Send the report to Telegram, show it here, or both. Start building on approve starts the build as soon as you approve an item. Ask before every deploy keeps the second approval before anything ships.

targets.title: Create
targets.description: Create saves the task and it runs on schedule. Create & run now also starts the first review straight away.

targets.title: Close the form
targets.description: Click Cancel to throw the draft away.

targets.title: The approvals inbox
targets.description: When something is waiting, a shield with a count appears in the command bar. Click it to open the inbox. It stays hidden while nothing needs you.

targets.title: Tasks & approvals
targets.description: Click Tasks & approvals. This is the older build/test task queue, where each task can require your approval before it runs.

targets.title: The task queue
targets.description: Executing, pending and recently completed tasks are listed here. Select one to see its details and pre-fire checklist on the right.

targets.title: Pause autonomy
targets.description: Pause in the page header stops autonomous task execution until you resume. It's the quickest brake if something looks wrong.

targets.title: Your document tree
targets.description: Everything lives in this tree: docs, folders and uploaded files. Drag rows to reorder them or drop one onto a folder to move it. Favourites and recently opened docs are listed above the tree.

targets.title: Create, upload, import
targets.description: The four icons create a doc, a folder, upload files and import from Notion, a ZIP or a URL. New items go into the folder you have open.

targets.title: Sort the tree
targets.description: Manual keeps your drag-and-drop order. Name and Updated sort automatically. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

targets.title: Search everything
targets.description: Type roadmap. Search covers titles, doc text and the text extracted from uploaded PDFs and Office files. Press Esc to clear it.

targets.title: Trash, not gone
targets.description: Deleting moves a doc to Trash. Open it here to restore an item or remove it for good.

targets.title: The folder view
targets.description: The main area shows the open folder: its item count, New doc, New folder and Upload. Imported Notion databases show up as folders with a property table.

targets.title: Switch to the table view
targets.description: Click Table. Each folder remembers its own view: List, Table (sortable columns, including database properties) or Grid cards.

targets.title: Open the importer
targets.description: Click ⤓ (Import from Notion / ZIP / URL).

targets.title: Three sources
targets.description: Notion (API) pulls pages live, Notion export ZIP reads an export file, and From URL downloads a single file. Imports go into the folder you have open (Into:).

targets.title: Find pages to import
targets.description: Type a page name. With no saved Notion connection, paste an internal-integration token (used for this import only) and share the pages with that integration in Notion. Press Search to list the pages and databases it can see, then tick the ones you want.

targets.title: Or use an export ZIP
targets.description: Click Notion export ZIP. This option needs no token.

targets.title: Export, then drop
targets.description: In Notion, go to Settings → Export → Markdown & CSV (include subpages), then drop the .zip here. Pages become docs, subpages become folders, databases become folders with a property table, and images are stored locally.

targets.title: Close the importer
targets.description: Click ✕. A running import keeps going, and a chip in the sidebar shows its progress.

targets.title: Your notes live here too
targets.description: Existing notes are copied into a Notes folder without touching the originals, and a JSON backup is written first. After that they stay in sync both ways: an agent editing a note updates the doc, and editing the doc writes back to the note. If you map a databas

targets.title: The Projects page
targets.description: This toolbar controls everything below it: the layout, filters, search, sort and + Project. Projects show as cards with their status, priority and task progress.

targets.title: Filter the board
targets.description: Tasks switches to the board of every task. AI Projects shows projects tagged for AI work. All / Active / Completed / Paused filter by status.

targets.title: Show only active work
targets.description: Click Active.

targets.title: Search projects
targets.description: Type website. Search matches project names, descriptions and types, and the Sort menu next to it orders cards by status, name, priority or recent activity.

targets.title: Back to everything
targets.description: Click All to clear the status filter.

targets.title: Adding a project
targets.description: + Project opens a short form: a name and a description. Change DB picks which Notion database backs Projects, if you keep them in Notion.

targets.title: Two layouts
targets.description: ⊞ shows projects as a card grid. ⫏ shows a kanban board grouped by status.

targets.title: Open the kanban
targets.description: Click ⫏ (Kanban View).

targets.title: Status columns
targets.description: Columns run Not Started → In Progress → Review / Waiting → Paused → Completed → Cancelled. Drag a project card to another column to change its status. Column edges can be dragged to resize them.

targets.title: Back to the grid
targets.description: Click ⊞ to return to cards. In the grid, Hide Sub-Projects tidies nested projects away.

targets.title: Open the task board
targets.description: Click Tasks.

targets.title: Task filters
targets.description: The counters show active and done tasks. Filter by priority here. Assignee and department filters appear once tasks have them.

targets.title: Search tasks
targets.description: Type invoice to narrow the board to matching tasks.

targets.title: Show finished work
targets.description: Tick Show done. Done tasks are hidden by default; this adds a Done column.

targets.title: Drag to change status
targets.description: Columns are Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Review / Blocked (plus Done). Drag a card between columns to change its status, or click it to open the detail.

targets.title: The Autonomous column
targets.description: Drop a task here to hand it to an agent. It's flagged for autonomous work and goes through a preflight check and your approval before work starts. Its status column doesn't change.

targets.title: Adding a task
targets.description: + Task opens a form with title, description, status and priority. Agents can add tasks too, and Notion sync brings in tasks from your Notion database.

targets.title: The workspace bar
targets.description: Everything on this page belongs to the workspace picked on the left of this bar. The rest of the bar controls the preview: server status, device width, route, reload and more actions.

targets.title: Open the picker
targets.description: Click the workspace name to list your workspaces.

targets.title: Find a workspace
targets.description: Type site. Recently used workspaces are listed first. The rest follow under All.

targets.title: Adding a workspace
targets.description: + Add workspace asks for a project type (web, app, document, PDF or presentation) and a local folder, with your recent folders one click away. It registers the folder; your files aren't changed.

targets.title: What a workspace gives you
targets.description: The folder's files become editable here, the workspace agent works only inside that folder, and kanban tasks for the matching project show up alongside it.

targets.title: The dev server
targets.description: This pill shows the preview server: Start, then Ready or Error. Clicking Start detects the framework, installs dependencies if they're missing, and runs the dev server for the preview.

targets.title: Preview at phone width
targets.description: Click the phone icon. The preview frame narrows to a phone width, and the tablet and desktop icons switch it back.

targets.title: Back to desktop
targets.description: Click the monitor icon to return to full width.

targets.title: Jump to a route
targets.description: Type a path such as /pricing and press Enter to open it in the preview. The ⟲ button next to it reloads the preview.

targets.title: Chat or Preview
targets.description: On a phone, the chat and the preview share the screen. Switch between them here.

targets.title: More actions
targets.description: Click ….

targets.title: What's in the menu
targets.description: Versions lists Git checkpoints. Files, code, diff & components opens the workbench, and Terminal & logs shows the raw dev server. You can also restart or stop the server, turn on auto-start, run Visual verify screenshots, split the preview, and switch the proj

targets.title: Select mode
targets.description: With a workspace running, the preview header has a Select button. Turn it on, then click any element in the preview to pick it. Press Esc to leave select mode.

targets.title: Describe the change
targets.description: The chat shows the selected element as context. Write what you want (“make this button gold and larger”) and press ⌘/Ctrl+Enter. The agent edits files in the workspace and the preview picks up the change.

targets.title: The Voice page
targets.description: This is the voice terminal. The header shows whether a voice session is LIVE or OFFLINE and which speech provider is in use. The tour won't start a call or use your microphone.

targets.title: Finish voice setup
targets.description: Voice isn't ready yet, and this card shows the one step missing: setting up local voice, or allowing the microphone. Local voice is the default: it runs privately on your computer with no keys. Cloud voice (Robovoice) is an optional, free choice for when your

targets.title: Tour first, then set up
targets.description: Click outside the card to continue the tour. The card comes back each new session until voice is ready, so you can finish setup straight after the tour.

targets.title: Which voice is active
targets.description: The provider badge names the speech stack this session will use and warns when something is missing, such as a key or a stopped local voice engine. Hover it for details.

targets.title: Session controls
targets.description: Connect starts a voice session. Mic mutes or unmutes it. Talk is push-to-talk with local Whisper. The picker chooses which agent or coding CLI answers, and ⌗ Terminal shows its live activity.

targets.title: Transcript and log
targets.description: What you and the agent say appears here, with the system log underneath. ▶ Terminal swaps the transcript for the answering CLI's terminal.

targets.title: The control deck
targets.description: The footer repeats the essentials: CONNECT / DISCONNECT, the agent picker and the LOCAL STT record button.

targets.title: Open voice settings
targets.description: Click ⚙ (Model & voice settings).

targets.title: Local or cloud voice
targets.description: Local voice is the default: Whisper and Kokoro or Piper run on this machine, so audio never leaves it. Ticks show which local models are present. Cloud voice (Robovoice) is optional and free; nothing switches to it unless you pick it.

targets.title: Who answers
targets.description: The voice route picks the brain. Gateway Agent uses the full reply pipeline (needs the LiveKit stack). Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex start that CLI and read its reply aloud.

targets.title: The voice itself
targets.description: TTS Provider and Voice Model pick how the agent sounds. The Wake Word switch turns the voice agent's wake word on or off.

targets.title: Test, then save
targets.description: Refresh and Test (smoke) check that speech-to-text and text-to-speech respond before you rely on them. Save Voice Stack and Save Configuration apply your changes.

targets.title: Close settings
targets.description: Click ✕ to close without saving.

targets.title: The microphone switch
targets.description: Wake words need the microphone, and InfiniBot never opens it until you turn on Listen for wake word. The badge at the top shows LISTENING, IDLE or OFF.

targets.title: Say “hey infinibot”
targets.description: “hey infinibot” and “live action” are fixed phrases that open Live Action from anywhere, with no tab or agent name needed. Keep Always on ticked, or add your own phrases.

targets.title: Navigate by voice
targets.description: Every page gets a “hey <page>” trigger. Rename or disable them here. Agents get “hey <agent>” triggers too.

targets.title: Your own commands
targets.description: Add command binds any phrase to an action: switch tab, open the voice panel, run a workflow or dispatch a UI action.

targets.title: Holographic HUD
targets.description: HUD switches the page to a full-screen holographic view: the voice blob in the centre, with running agents and node hardware around the edges. Leave it from inside the HUD, and your choice is remembered.

targets.title: System modules
targets.description: The System panel shows the Vision Engine, Microphone, Camera and Audio Engine at a glance, with a log counter. Collapse it with the arrow for more room.

targets.title: Watch the agent work
targets.description: Click ⌗ Terminal to float the cloud terminal: a draggable panel that shows the answering agent's live activity.

targets.title: One card per channel
targets.description: Each card is a channel the gateway can run. Enabled channels are listed first. The pill in the corner reads Not configured, Connected and so on at a glance.

targets.title: Channel health
targets.description: At the bottom is the raw status snapshot from the gateway, for when you need to debug a channel that won't start.

targets.title: Link with a QR code
targets.description: Connect (Show QR) shows a code. On your phone, open WhatsApp → Linked Devices and scan it, and it links by itself. Relink starts over with a fresh code, Wait for scan keeps watching, and Logout unlinks.

targets.title: Every client thread in one list
targets.description: Client conversations from Telegram, email, WhatsApp, Discord and Instagram land here. The pills show which channels are ready and which still need setup. Filter the list by assignment or by channel.

targets.title: Approve before it sends
targets.description: Open a thread to read it and reply. Replies an agent drafts can wait as pending approval: Approve & send delivers one, Reject drops it. The count to approve shows at the top of the list.

targets.title: Three tabs
targets.description: Tools are built into InfiniBot. Skills teach agents how to use them. MCPs are the extra servers that add more tools.

targets.title: Native tools
targets.description: Click Tools.

targets.title: What agents can already do
targets.description: Kanban, files, web, browser, memory, cron, sessions, workflows, notes and research. Each card shows its transport, its tool count and whether it's running.

targets.title: MCP servers
targets.description: Click MCPs.

targets.title: The MCP server
targets.description: Shows whether InfiniBot's MCP server is running, on which port, and how many servers are enabled. Restart, Stop and Start control it.

targets.title: Configured servers
targets.description: Every MCP server this gateway knows, grouped by category. Browse registry searches public servers and Add custom takes any command. Both add a server, so they aren't clicked here.

targets.title: Quick Install
targets.description: InfiniBot is an MCP server too. Point Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client here and it can use InfiniBot's tools, sub-agents and boards.

targets.title: Local, LAN or Tailscale
targets.description: Pick where the client runs. Local is this machine. LAN exposes the gateway to your network, so turn on a key. Tailscale is the secure way in from outside.

targets.title: Pick your client
targets.description: Choose the client and your OS: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Continue, Codex CLI, OpenCode or a generic JSON or HTTP setup.

targets.title: Copy the snippet
targets.description: Paste this into the config file shown under it, or run it for Claude Code. The Claude Code button in the status bar writes the entry for you.

targets.title: Discover
targets.description: Featured integrations you can add in one click, filtered by category.

targets.title: Search integrations
targets.description: Type github.

targets.title: Servers inside plugins
targets.description: Plugins can bundle MCP servers. Whiteboard, for example, brings the Excalidraw canvas tools. They're listed under the plugin's What it adds and run only while the plugin is on.

targets.title: The Skills page
targets.description: At a glance: active skills, pending drafts and healing proposals, and what you accepted or rejected in the last week.

targets.title: Active skills
targets.description: Click Active Skills.

targets.title: Discover skills
targets.description: Each skill is a SKILL.md folder that teaches an agent a task. Filter by category or status: Enabled, Needs setup (missing a binary or key) or Disabled.

targets.title: Search
targets.description: Search by name, description, trigger or requirement. Type github.

targets.title: Write your own
targets.description: Create skill opens a form: name, description, when to use it, allowed tools and step-by-step instructions. It saves a new SKILL.md your agents can use.

targets.title: Self-generated skills
targets.description: The agent distils skills from its own completed runs and refines them once they're used enough. Run Self-Improve refines eligible skills on demand.

targets.title: Drafts
targets.description: Click Drafts.

targets.title: Review before promoting
targets.description: Skill candidates generated from completed runs. Accept one to install it, or reject it. With auto-approval on, accepted drafts go straight to self-generated skills.

targets.title: Healing
targets.description: Click Healing.

targets.title: Fixes for existing skills
targets.description: When a task fails because a skill was wrong, InfiniBot proposes a correction. Compare it with the current skill, then apply or reject it.

targets.title: Settings
targets.description: Click Settings to control when the system drafts and proposes new skills.

targets.title: The Plugins page
targets.description: This is where plugins live. The counters show how many are installed, how many are on, and how many more are available to add.

targets.title: Filter what you see
targets.description: All, Installed, Enabled or Available. Click Installed to see what's already on this gateway.

targets.title: Categories and trust
targets.description: Narrow the list to Apps, Channels, Integrations or Developer tools. The trust chips separate first-party plugins (made by InfiniBot) from verified and community publishers.

targets.title: Search the store
targets.description: Search matches names, channels and tags. Type infinitrade.

targets.title: The plugin's page
targets.description: Its name, publisher, version and status. The rest of this page is organised into sections, which the next walkthrough covers.

targets.title: One page, nine sections
targets.description: Overview, What it adds, Permissions, Settings, Appearance, Health & Logs, Data, Versions and Uninstall. Click a section to jump to it.

targets.title: What it adds
targets.description: Click What it adds.

targets.title: Permissions
targets.description: Click Permissions.

targets.title: What it may do
targets.description: Each permission shows its risk and whether it's granted. Gated permissions, like Infinitrade's gated:orders for placing orders, stay Off by default until you grant them yourself.

targets.title: Health & Logs
targets.description: Click Health & Logs. On a narrow screen, scroll the section bar sideways or just scroll down.

targets.title: Is it working?
targets.description: Health, its HTTP routes, background services and recent log lines. Restart plugin services is live. A Full reload restarts the gateway.

targets.title: Data and versions
targets.description: Data shows the plugin's storage folder, with export, import and clear. Versions shows where it came from and offers update or roll back when available.

targets.title: The on/off switch
targets.description: Turning a plugin on or off restarts the gateway to load or unload its code. That takes a few seconds, and InfiniBot asks you to confirm first. A paid plugin you haven't bought shows Buy instead of the switch.
keywords: What turning a plugin on gives you

targets.title: Take the tour
targets.description: An enabled plugin that ships a guided track shows Take the tour on its card and its page. It starts that plugin's walkthrough right here.
keywords: What turning a plugin on gives you

targets.title: Jump there
targets.description: Click the card, or press Enter, to open the page.

targets.title: The Mobile page
targets.description: Everything for getting InfiniBot onto a phone lives here: the Android APK, a development client, and instructions for building the app yourself.

targets.title: Android app (APK)
targets.description: Once an APK is published on this gateway, this card shows its version, a Download APK button and a QR code. Until then it shows the one command that publishes one.

targets.title: Install & Connect
targets.description: Click Install & Connect in the Setup menu.

targets.title: Your connection details
targets.description: The gateway address, its token (masked) and a short connection code. The QR code encodes an infinibot://connect?url=…&token=… link the app reads to fill in the connection for you.

targets.title: Three ways in
targets.description: Dev client (Metro) runs the app's JavaScript from this machine. Build the app signs your own APK or IPA. Web Preview runs the mobile app in your browser. Click Dev client (Metro).

targets.title: Pick a connection mode
targets.description: Tunnel works across networks but is slower. LAN is fast on the same Wi-Fi. Localhost is for a simulator on this machine. Tailscale works across your tailnet.

targets.title: The gateway URL
targets.description: Pre-filled from this gateway's WebSocket address. If your phone is on another network, paste a public URL, such as a Cloudflare Tunnel or Tailscale Serve address.

targets.title: Start Metro and scan
targets.description: Start Expo dev server starts Metro and shows a QR. Scan it from the InfiniBot dev client. Expo Go from the app stores won't load this app, because it uses native modules.

targets.title: Build the app
targets.description: Click Build the app.
keywords: Build it yourself, or preview it

targets.title: Android and iOS builds
targets.description: Android: build locally with Gradle or in Expo's cloud with EAS, then publish the APK so it appears in the card above. iOS: EAS signs an IPA with your Apple account.
keywords: Build it yourself, or preview it

targets.title: Web Preview
targets.description: Click Web Preview.
keywords: Build it yourself, or preview it

targets.title: The app in your browser
targets.description: This is the web build of the mobile app shipped with your install. It's a quick way to try a screen without a phone.
keywords: Build it yourself, or preview it

targets.title: Devices
targets.description: Browsers, phones and nodes pair with the gateway. New requests wait under Pending until you approve or reject them. Approved devices move to Paired.

targets.title: Nodes
targets.description: Nodes are paired machines that can run commands for your agents. Each one shows here with its live links.

targets.title: The Users page
targets.description: Until the first account exists, every connection is treated as the implicit admin. Once you create a user, only accounts with the admin role can manage users.

targets.title: Look at the New User form
targets.description: Click New User. You'll look at the form and cancel. Nothing is created.

targets.title: Role
targets.description: admin can create, edit and delete users. user can change only their own profile. The Gateway password field is how InfiniBot tells which account a connection belongs to.

targets.title: Fence in the agent
targets.description: Lock agent to home + allowed directories keeps this user's agents inside their home folder and the folders you list.

targets.title: Limit the pages
targets.description: Allowed pages lists the only pages this user may open, for example chat, projects. Leave it empty to allow all.

targets.title: Cancel
targets.description: Click Cancel to close the form without creating anyone.

targets.title: Exec approvals
targets.description: Decides whether agents may run shell commands on the gateway or on a node. A command runs only when the policy, the allowlist and, if needed, your approval all agree.

targets.title: Security and Ask
targets.description: Security: Deny blocks everything, Allowlist runs only listed binaries, Full allows anything. Ask: Off, On miss (prompt when the allowlist doesn't match) or Always. If nobody can answer the prompt, Ask fallback decides.

targets.title: Business HQ
targets.description: HQ answers one question: what moves the business today. Every number, card and row on this page opens the list behind it. Refresh re-reads the live board.

targets.title: Daily progress
targets.description: Tasks you complete on the board count toward a daily target (5 by default), with a streak and a weekly total. Recap shows what was closed today. Bulk completions are never counted.

targets.title: The KPI strip
targets.description: Active work, overdue, blocked, needs you, pipeline, active clients, active projects and open risks. Click any tile to open the items behind the number.

targets.title: Executive lens
targets.description: Command opens on Executive: only exceptions, priorities and decisions. Today, This week, Business health and the CEO queue each list what only you can move.

targets.title: Run the organization
targets.description: Operations shows the operating snapshot, then everything that needs attention, the portfolio, workload and system quality. Executive filters for you. Operations shows the whole org.

targets.title: Clients
targets.description: The CRM has four tabs: Clients, Revenue, Pipeline and Activity. The cards above them total clients, active clients, MRR, average deal and churn.

targets.title: Search clients
targets.description: Type acme to filter the list. The status filter next to it narrows by prospect, active, paused or churned.

targets.title: Switch the view
targets.description: Click Table. The list also shows as a grid or a kanban board grouped by stage.

targets.title: Open Revenue
targets.description: Click Revenue to see the revenue logged against your clients for the active agency, with the running total.

targets.title: Log an opportunity
targets.description: + New Opportunity opens a form for the type, stage, value, score and next step. When one is won, it can be converted into a project.

targets.title: Five lead sections
targets.description: Overview, Generation (scrape and search for leads), Qualifier, Pipeline and Timeline (opens, clicks and replies per lead).

targets.title: Open the Qualifier
targets.description: Click Qualifier.

targets.title: The HoloCanvas library
targets.description: Every saved walkthrough canvas in one place, with a count. The buttons on the right create new ones.

targets.title: Filter by tag
targets.description: Tags come from the canvases themselves. Pick one to narrow the gallery, or All to see everything.

targets.title: The gallery
targets.description: Each card shows the title, how many cards and scenes it has, its tags, and ✓ baked once narration audio exists. Canvases your agents save, such as work reviews, land here too.

targets.title: The preview pane
targets.description: Select a canvas and it plays here, with actions to narrate, share, export and re-show it.

targets.title: Load the examples
targets.description: Click Load examples to add two short example canvases. They're neutral and only ever added once.

targets.title: Open a canvas
targets.description: Click a canvas card to preview it.

targets.title: Play it inline
targets.description: The walkthrough plays here scene by scene. When it ends it starts again from the first scene.

targets.title: Share and export
targets.description: Copy Link copies a /canvas/<id> share link, which keeps working even with this plugin off. Download HTML saves a single-file export you can open anywhere.

targets.title: Narrate and re-show
targets.description: Bake Narration generates per-scene audio with your voice provider. Re-emit shows the canvas again as an on-screen overlay. Delete removes it from the library.

targets.title: Build from a report
targets.description: Click From report.

targets.title: Pick a report
targets.description: Your reports are listed here. Converting one turns each section into a card and a scene, and saves the result to the library.

targets.title: Close
targets.description: Click Close.

targets.title: Paste a payload
targets.description: Click + New to save a canvas from its JSON payload.

targets.title: Cancel
targets.description: Click Cancel to close without saving.

targets.title: Your content pages
targets.description: One page per surface: an Instagram account, a YouTube channel, a blog. Each card shows the page's reach at a glance.

targets.title: Find a page
targets.description: Search by name, then narrow by business or surface with the two filters beside it.

targets.title: Filter by surface
targets.description: Show only Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, a blog, LinkedIn and so on.

targets.title: Start a new page
targets.description: Click New page to open the setup wizard.

targets.title: The wizard's steps
targets.description: Basics, Goals, Connections and Brand voice. Instagram pages add an Instagram step and an optional ManyChat step for DM automation.

targets.title: Name the page
targets.description: Type a name. You also pick the surface, handle, URL, business and an optional owner agent here.

targets.title: What Create page does
targets.description: On the last step, Create page saves the page and provisions its Scripts, Videos, Content and Ideas databases. Connect Instagram afterwards from the page's Integrations tab.

targets.title: Close the wizard
targets.description: Click × to leave without creating anything.

targets.title: Start with your data
targets.description: Intelligence analyses your own reels. Until you import some, this is the starting point.

targets.title: Import an Instagram CSV
targets.description: Export your reels as CSV from Meta Business Suite, then import it here by file path on the gateway machine, optionally for one account. Accounts and YouTube in the header add more sources.

targets.title: Score and transcribe
targets.description: Once reels are in, Transcribe writes a script for each one and Score all rates hook, value and viral potential, then ranks it against viral-format benchmarks for your niche. Filter by scored, unscored or no script, and sort by views, saves, score or tier.

targets.title: What's on now
targets.description: The hero shows the block you're in and the time left, or the next block and when it starts. With nothing planned it says Ready when you are.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Today's score
targets.description: Compliance is how much of today's planned block time you kept. Next to it are focus minutes today and your day streak.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Act on the current block
targets.description: During a block you get Check in and Abort. Otherwise + New block starts a new one.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Running late? Start from now
targets.description: Start from now shifts every remaining block so the day starts right now, keeping each block's length.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Log what just happened
targets.description: Type a line here. Enter logs it against the active block, and L jumps here from anywhere on the page.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Pick a category
targets.description: The category defaults to the active block's. Change it when the entry belongs somewhere else. The tour leaves the entry unsaved.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Open the Timeline
targets.description: Click Timeline. It lays today's blocks and logs on the clock.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Work that logs itself
targets.description: With auto-log on, agent runs and finished kanban tasks land here and count against the active block. Your first activity also starts the day.
keywords: Read your day at a glance

targets.title: Open Blocks
targets.description: Click Blocks. It lists every block you have, or starter presets when you have none.

targets.title: Start from a preset
targets.description: With no blocks yet, a preset fills the day with sensible blocks you can edit afterwards. Once you have blocks, this area shows them as a board or a list.

targets.title: Create a block
targets.description: Click the button to open the block editor.

targets.title: Name it
targets.description: Give the block a short label you'll recognise on the timeline.

targets.title: Choose the days
targets.description: Pick the days the block repeats, or use Weekdays, Weekends or Every day.

targets.title: How strict is it?
targets.description: Hard lock blocks notifications during the block. Non-negotiable means missing it breaks your streak. Untick Enabled to pause a block without deleting it.

targets.title: Add a routine item
targets.description: Routines are the habits you run inside a block every day it runs. Click + Add routine item.

targets.title: Write the habit
targets.description: Type a checklist item. Enter adds another one. You tick these off inside the block each day.

targets.title: Saving a block
targets.description: Create block saves it to your schedule. You can also link the block to a project or task. This tour cancels instead.

targets.title: Cancel the draft
targets.description: Click Cancel to close the editor without saving.

targets.title: The active template
targets.description: This strip shows which template your day came from, and Modified once you change it. It appears on Timeline and Blocks.

targets.title: Save a layout
targets.description: Save as template snapshots all your current blocks under a name, like "Workday" or "Build sprint Mondays".

targets.title: Load a template
targets.description: Click Load… to browse your templates and the built-in presets.

targets.title: Replace or append
targets.description: Each template can replace your current layout or append its blocks alongside what you have. Manage lets you rename and delete your own templates.

targets.title: Close it
targets.description: Click Close.

targets.title: Open Score
targets.description: Click Score.

targets.title: Day and week scores
targets.description: Today's compliance, the week and your streak sit on top. Below are trends, time logged per category and which blocks you keep or slip.

targets.title: Open Settings
targets.description: Click Settings. The keyboard shortcut is 4.

targets.title: Telegram block messages
targets.description: Push block starts, slips and daily reviews to Telegram through your gateway's bot. Set a chat ID here to send them somewhere other than the default chat.

targets.title: The AI assistant
targets.description: When it's on, the assistant can plan tomorrow and write a daily review, with your blocks and kanban as context.

targets.title: Day window and quiet hours
targets.description: Set when your day starts and ends, how often probes nudge you, and quiet hours that mute Telegram and audio nudges.

targets.title: Five slots, no more
targets.description: The counter shows how many of your five slots are filled. The hard limit keeps you honest about what you're actually working on.

targets.title: Rank them
targets.description: Drag an item into a numbered slot, drag to reorder, and use × to take it off the board.

targets.title: Available items
targets.description: Your kanban projects and tasks. Search, filter by type, or switch to a kanban view.

targets.title: Show only projects
targets.description: Click Projects to narrow the list.

targets.title: Quick add
targets.description: The + button opens a search box to add any task or project to Focus.

targets.title: Search for something
targets.description: Type at least two characters. Clicking a result adds it to your board; this tour stops before that.

targets.title: Welcome to InfiniCode
targets.description: InfiniCode is a monospace twin of the Agent Mesh map. It reads the same live mesh data, so what you see here matches the isometric map.

targets.title: The mesh map
targets.description: The header counts nodes and agents and shows ◉ live while the gateway stream is connected. The map refreshes every few seconds and applies live updates in between.

targets.title: Device nodes
targets.description: Each box is a node on the mesh: this gateway (the hub) plus any paired devices. Click a node to filter the agents to that machine and to aim spawns and the coder at it.

targets.title: The 10 sectors
targets.description: Agents land in a sector by what they are doing: editing and shell work in Engineering Bay, reading and search in Observatory, orchestrators in Command Atrium, idle agents in Agent Quarters. ● is a worker, ◆ an orchestrator.

targets.title: Mesh messages
targets.description: Messages between agents and nodes scroll here, newest first, with a throughput sparkline and a per-minute count. An empty log just means the mesh is idle.

targets.title: Live hardware
targets.description: CPU, memory, GPU and disk meters stream for the selected node, and default to this machine. Select another node to see its hardware.

targets.title: Open the isometric map
targets.description: iso map → opens the full Agent Mesh page with the same nodes and agents drawn in 3D.

targets.title: Switch to the fleet
targets.description: Click infinicode fleet. The map is replaced by the list of servers that run the infinicode CLI.

targets.title: One row per server
targets.description: A server appears once it pushes its status to this gateway. Each row shows CPU and memory, when it last reported and its latest maintenance result (✓ or ✗). Servers are grouped by site once there is more than one.

targets.title: Back to agent ops
targets.description: Click agent ops to return to the mesh map. Plugins › InfiniCode › Appearance lets you choose which view the page opens on.

targets.title: The devices panel
targets.description: Every node on the mesh is listed with its role, online status, agent count, capabilities and advertised URL.

targets.title: The command bar
targets.description: The bar at the bottom spawns agents on the selected device. With no node selected, runs go to this gateway (local).

targets.title: Pick an agent
targets.description: Choose which roster agent runs the task: coder, opus, tester, architect, backend, reviewer or doc.

targets.title: Draft a task
targets.description: Type a task for the agent. This only fills the field; nothing runs until you press spawn or Enter.

targets.title: Spawn the run
targets.description: spawn starts a real session for the agent on the selected device. It then appears as a glyph on the map and moves between sectors as it works.

targets.title: The embedded coder
targets.description: The CODER panel is a live terminal running Claude Code (claude) on the selected device. Pick another node and the terminal moves to that machine.

targets.title: Hand off to a coder
targets.description: The field above the terminal spawns the coder agent with a task instead of typing into the terminal yourself. Agents can also launch Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode runs with their claude_coder, codex_coder and opencode_coder tools; those runs show up on the ma

targets.title: The command header
targets.description: The header shows which trading sessions are open, your open P&L and balance, and the account switcher. Click P&L to jump to the journal.

targets.title: Twelve sections
targets.description: Every section has its own sidebar entry and URL (/infinitrade/journal, …). Terminal is the default.

targets.title: Analysis, not advice
targets.description: Infinitrade is for market analysis and education. Orders stay off until the owner allows them, and each one needs your typed confirmation.

targets.title: Open Settings
targets.description: Click Settings (Connection & Safety).

targets.title: The gated:orders permission
targets.description: Place orders is the host permission gated:orders. It's off on every install and after an import. Only the owner can turn it on, here or in Setup › Plugins › Infinitrade › Permissions. A per-order lot cap (1 by default) applies.

targets.title: Connect TradeLocker
targets.description: Your TradeLocker login is encrypted on this gateway and never shown again. Choose Demo to practise with a paper account before you ever use Live. Test checks the login without saving it.

targets.title: Open the Scanner
targets.description: Click Scanner.

targets.title: Open the live feed
targets.description: Click Signals.

targets.title: Open the Journal
targets.description: Click Journal.

targets.title: Open Accounts
targets.description: Click Accounts.

targets.title: Open the Toolkit
targets.description: Click Toolkit.

targets.title: Open Knowledge
targets.description: Click Knowledge, the market knowledge hub.

targets.title: Open the Calendar
targets.description: Click Calendar.

targets.title: Open Research
targets.description: Click Research.

targets.title: The whiteboard toolbar
targets.description: Boards, templates, save, clear, refresh and open-in-a-new-tab live here, above the canvas.

targets.title: Connected
targets.description: Connected means the canvas engine is live, so changes from you and your agents land on the same scene.

targets.title: The canvas
targets.description: An infinite Excalidraw canvas. Hold the mouse wheel or Space while dragging to pan; use the zoom controls in the corner.

targets.title: Your saved boards
targets.description: Click Boards to see every canvas you've saved.

targets.title: Open or delete a board
targets.description: Click a board to load it onto the canvas. The bin icon deletes it. Boards are stored in the plugin's data folder.

targets.title: Start from a template
targets.description: Click Templates.

targets.title: Pick a starting layout
targets.description: Templates are grouped by category: blank, flowchart, mind map, wireframe and kanban. Picking one replaces what's on the canvas, so save first.

targets.title: Save to Boards
targets.description: Save to Boards asks for a name and stores the current canvas.

targets.title: Clear Canvas
targets.description: Clear Canvas wipes every element after a confirmation. Saved boards are not affected.

targets.title: Canvas Architect
targets.description: This panel talks to the canvas agent, a diagram specialist. If it's collapsed, the 🎨 button opens it.

targets.title: Ideas to start from
targets.description: Click a suggestion to put it in the prompt, or write your own.

targets.title: Describe the diagram
targets.description: Type what you want drawn.

targets.title: Canvas in the command bar
targets.description: Click Canvas in the command bar. On a phone it sits under More (⋯).

targets.title: A floating canvas
targets.description: The same canvas, over whatever page you're on. Drag the header to move it, drag an edge to resize, and minimise it when you need the page back.

targets.title: Close it
targets.description: Click × to close the floater, or click Canvas again. The canvas itself is unchanged.

targets.title: The Clinic page
targets.description: OmniClinic brings medical research intelligence, a cited research engine and your clinic's databases into one place.

targets.title: Read the safety notice
targets.description: Every OmniClinic page carries this notice. It is a research tool, not clinical decision support: summaries can be wrong, and a qualified clinician makes every clinical decision.

targets.title: Four counters
targets.description: Cached feed articles and the last sync, research briefings and open contradictions, your databases and record count, and how many sources answered the last sweep. Off means offline mode: cached data only.

targets.title: Latest research
targets.description: The newest cached articles, each tagged by type (paper, preprint, trial, safety notice, news).

targets.title: Clinic mode
targets.description: Admins see Make this the start page. It opens OmniClinic instead of the dashboard when InfiniBot starts. You can also set it in Plugins › OmniClinic.

targets.title: Open Research
targets.description: Click Open Research to go to the feed and the research engine.

targets.title: You're on Research
targets.description: Research also has its own sidebar entry under Clinic.

targets.title: Two modes
targets.description: Research has two modes: the Intelligence feed of new publications and the Research engine for your own questions. Click Intelligence feed.

targets.title: Free public sources
targets.description: The feed pulls from PubMed, Europe PMC, medRxiv, bioRxiv, ClinicalTrials.gov, openFDA and health news, then caches the articles on this gateway.

targets.title: Filter the cache
targets.description: Type a topic to filter the cached articles. The filter only searches what is already stored.

targets.title: Filter by type
targets.description: Narrow the list to papers, preprints, trials, safety notices or news.

targets.title: Specialties
targets.description: Once articles are cached, specialty chips with counts appear under the toolbar. Pick one to see only that specialty.

targets.title: Refresh sweeps every source
targets.description: Refresh asks every source for new items right now. It's disabled in offline mode. A background refresh can also be set in the plugin settings (every 15 minutes or more).

targets.title: Switch to the engine
targets.description: Click Research engine.

targets.title: Ask a clinical question
targets.description: Describe the clinical or scientific question, not the patient. Type one to try it; nothing runs until you press Run research.

targets.title: Identifiers are removed
targets.description: Names, record numbers, dates of birth, emails and phone numbers are removed before anything is searched, and the page lists what it removed. Still, keep patient details out of questions.

targets.title: Run research
targets.description: The engine splits the question into searches, reads the sources and writes a cited Evidence briefing, with live progress for each stage.

targets.title: Open contradictions
targets.description: When sources disagree, the engine records a contradiction with a severity. Mark each one Resolve or Dismiss after you've checked it.

targets.title: Research briefings
targets.description: Every finished run is saved here so you can come back to it.

targets.title: Clinic databases
targets.description: Your clinic's own tables, such as conditions, formulary, protocols and follow-ups. They're kept separate from the business databases, and rows stay on this gateway.

targets.title: The table
targets.description: The selected database shows every property as a column, with its type under the name. Click a row to open it in the editor.

targets.title: Filter rows
targets.description: Type to filter rows across every column. This only changes the view.

targets.title: Open Properties
targets.description: Click Properties to see the columns of this database.

targets.title: Typed, Notion-style properties
targets.description: Each property has a name and a type (text, number, date, select, multi-select, status, clinic role and more). Rename, retype, reorder or delete them here. The title property can't be deleted.

targets.title: Draft a new property
targets.description: Type a name to try it. The property is only added when you press Add.

targets.title: Close without adding
targets.description: Click the close button to leave without adding anything.

targets.title: Open Roles
targets.description: Click Roles. Clinic roles are the choices for role properties, such as who owns a follow-up.
keywords: Roles, new tables and patient data

targets.title: Built-in and custom roles
targets.description: Built-in roles can be renamed but not deleted, so role properties never point at a missing role. Your own roles can be deleted.
keywords: Roles, new tables and patient data

targets.title: Draft a role
targets.description: Type a role name to try the field. It's only added when you press Add role or Enter.
keywords: Roles, new tables and patient data

targets.title: New databases
targets.description: New database creates an empty table, one from a template, or one from a CSV file where the first row becomes the column names.
keywords: Roles, new tables and patient data

targets.title: Patient data stays here
targets.description: Rows can hold patient information. OmniClinic declares the phi permission, keeps its database on this gateway, and never logs row contents. Keep backups encrypted and limit who can sign in.
keywords: Roles, new tables and patient data

targets.title: Your product catalog
targets.description: Digital and physical inventory in one list. The header counts your items.
keywords: Find your way around the Catalog

targets.title: Catalog at a glance
targets.description: Active, Drafts, Out of stock and the total Catalog value, updated as you edit products.
keywords: Find your way around the Catalog

targets.title: Search the catalog
targets.description: Search matches name, SKU, tags and description.
keywords: Find your way around the Catalog

targets.title: Filter by type and status
targets.description: Narrow to digital, physical, service, bundle or subscription products, and to active, draft, out of stock or archived.
keywords: Find your way around the Catalog

targets.title: Switch to the list
targets.description: Click List for compact rows. Gallery shows product cards with media.
keywords: Find your way around the Catalog

targets.title: Bring products in from Notion
targets.description: Import from Notion binds one or more Notion databases as catalog sources; SKU, price and inventory columns map in automatically. Catalog rows use the Databases products role, so Notion sync keeps working.
keywords: Find your way around the Catalog

targets.title: New product
targets.description: Click New product.
keywords: Add a product to the Catalog

targets.title: Name it
targets.description: Only the name is required. Type one.
keywords: Add a product to the Catalog

targets.title: The essentials
targets.description: Add an SKU, the type, a price and a short description. Cost, inventory, vendor, media and a Stripe product id are edited afterwards in the product's inspector.
keywords: Add a product to the Catalog

targets.title: Creating it
targets.description: Create product saves it and opens it in the inspector. This tour cancels instead.
keywords: Add a product to the Catalog

targets.title: Cancel
targets.description: Click Cancel.
keywords: Add a product to the Catalog

targets.title: Official name
targets.description: Type the product's official working name.

targets.title: Validation stage
targets.description: Separate from status. It climbs from Idea, Prototype and Proof of Concept to Pilot, Paying Customer, Repeat Sales and Scaled.

targets.title: One accountable owner
targets.description: Every product needs exactly one product owner for commercial direction. A technical owner and a supporting owner are optional.

targets.title: The commercial case
targets.description: Further down: target customer, revenue model, problem solved, value proposition, pricing, the next product decision and the next action with an owner and date.

targets.title: Cancel
targets.description: Click Cancel to close without saving.

targets.title: Robovoice settings
targets.description: If you pick Cloud voice, your agents talk through Robovoice characters. This page is where you choose where Robovoice runs, map agents to characters and see usage.

targets.title: Which provider serves voice
targets.description: The top card shows which voice provider is active and whether it is ready. The same card appears in Setup › Voice.

targets.title: Connection
targets.description: Where Robovoice runs, its URL and the credentials this gateway uses to reach it. Nothing here takes effect until you press Save.

targets.title: Usage
targets.description: Cloud voice is free. Usage is measured only to keep it fair for everyone, and if it's busy you can switch to local voice in one click.

targets.title: Character mapping
targets.description: Each InfiniBot agent can speak as its own Robovoice character. Agents without a mapping use the default.

targets.title: Pipelines
targets.description: The effective STT → LLM → TTS chain for each mapped character. Pipelines are edited in the Robovoice dashboard; this card is read-only.

targets.title: InfiniBot tools for Robovoice
targets.description: Robovoice characters can call a curated set of InfiniBot tools through this MCP endpoint.

targets.title: The Robovoice URL
targets.description: For cloud this is https://robovoice.io; self-hosted is usually http://<host>:3011. Type it to try the field. It isn't saved until you press Save.

targets.title: Edge device id
targets.description: The name this gateway uses as a Robovoice edge device, for example infinibot-gateway.

targets.title: Edge token from robovoice login
targets.description: On cloud, run robovoice login in the Robovoice CLI and paste the rve_… edge token here. Self-hosted stacks with a strict device policy use the Device key field instead.

targets.title: Location and expressive tier
targets.description: An optional Robovoice location id applies that location's pipeline overrides.

targets.title: Test, then save
targets.description: Test connection checks Robovoice's health and character list only. Save stores the settings and secrets, then reloads characters and pipelines.

targets.title: The default character
targets.description: Agents without their own mapping speak as this character. Robovoice decides uses Robovoice's active character. The list fills in once Robovoice is connected.

targets.title: One row per agent
targets.description: Pick a character for any agent, such as main or an AI employee. A change is saved as soon as you pick. The Voice column shows the character's TTS provider and language.

targets.title: Self-host only labels
targets.description: Some models, such as openWakeWord's bundled wake words and Piper Lessac voices, are non-commercial. They're labelled Self-host only, and on a cloud deployment the warning turns red so you swap them before offering calls to others.

targets.title: Holder risk
targets.description: A deterministic 0–100 score from holder concentration, linked clusters, bundlers and snipers, dev and insiders, fresh wallets and token authorities. Analyze adds an AI read using your model.

targets.title: Wallet convergence
targets.description: Convergence ranks tokens that several of your tracked wallets bought within a time window. Each entry is scored, and an alert fires above your threshold.

targets.title: Tune the signal
targets.description: Set the minimum wallets (N), the window (T minutes), the minimum size and group weights. Intel-only wallets count for signals without being copied.

targets.title: Moving SOL
targets.description: SOL transfers, distribution and collection need the Transfer funds permission. Review transfer shows the details before anything is sent.

targets.title: Limits and dry run
targets.description: Strategy, scale, max SOL per trade, a daily cap, minimum liquidity, maximum price impact and TP/SL are checked before every write. Dry run records decisions without trading.
keywords: Copy Bot, alerts and the queue

targets.title: Recent alerts
